## What is XP?
XP (Experience Points) reflects consistent study effort.

### How to earn XP
Activity | XP |
|---|---|
| Complete a practice test | 30 |
| Complete a mock exam | 75 |
| Correct answer (practice) | 1 |
| Correct answer (mock) | 3 |

### High score bonuses | Variies. |
| Daily login | 10 |
| Study plan session completion | 30 |

### Streak multiplier
Longer active streaks increase XP gain.
Example: If base reward is 75 and multiplier is 1.75, awarded XP is 131 (rounded policy may vary).

### Level system
Each level requires more XP than the previous level. Level title bands provide milestone identity and motivation.

### Where to monitor progress
- Dashboard summary
- Profile page
- Post-session reward breakdown
- Leaderboard comparisons

## What are achievements?
Achievements are milestone badges for consistency, performance, and mastery.

### Category examples
- Milestones (activity counts)
- Performance (high scores)
- Streak (consecutive active days)
- Dedication (time and behavior patterns)
- Mastery (subject excellence)
- Hidden achievements (surprise unlocks)

### Rarity tiers
- Common
- Uncommon
- Rare
- Epic
- Legendary

### Tips to unlock efficiently
1. Prioritize consistency first.
2. Mix easy wins with long-term goals.
3. Review progress weekly and adjust focus.

content.body:
### What is UPCAT Simulator?
UPCAT Simulator is an online review platform designed to help students prepare for college entrance-style tests through guided study, targeted practice, and realistic exam simulation.
It gives you three study experiences:
1. **Practice Tests** for flexible learning sessions.
2. **Mock Exams** for realistic time-pressure assessment.
3. **Study Plan** for daily, personalized progress.

### What is the UPCAT?
The University of the Philippines College Admission Test (UPCAT) is a high-stakes admission exam used by the University of the Philippines system. It typically includes language, mathematics, science, and reading-heavy reasoning.
[info]
> The platform focuses on skill-building and exam readiness. It is not a replacement for school learning, but a structured companion.

### How this platform helps you prepare:
1. Build fundamentals first: You can start with easier practice sets and immediate feedback to understand concepts deeply.
2. Train speed and endurance: Once your foundation improves, you can add timers and transition to longer sessions.
3. Measure real readiness: Mock exams replicate stricter conditions so you can evaluate performance under pressure.
4. Track progress over time: Your dashboards and stats pages show trends, weak areas, and improvements.

### Main feature overview
Feature | Best For |
---|---|
Practice Test | Learning and drills (Low to medium) | Immediate or end-of-test feedback
Exam Readiness Checks | High | End-of-exam only
Study Plan | Daily guided progress | Medium | Session and module-based
Gamification | Motivation and consistency | N/A | Real-time XP/achievement updates
Your first 5 minutes | Open your dashboard.
Start a **short practice session** (20-30 questions). Keep timer optional on your first run. Turn on immediate feedback. Review mistakes and note 1-2 weak topics.
Platform disclaimer: UPCAT Simulator is an independent educational platform and is not affiliated with the University of the Philippines or the official UPCAT administration.

### Next steps
Read [How Practice Tests Work] (/help/article/how-practice-test-works)
Read [Navigating the Dashboard] (/help/article/navigating-dashboard)
Start your first practice session on [/practice] (/practice)

### Registration steps
1. Go to the registration page.
2. Enter your first name, last name, email, and password.
3. Confirm your password and submit.
4. Check your email for the verification link.

[Registration Form Placeholder] (/help-assets/screenshots/register-form.png)

### Email verification after registration:
1. Open your inbox.
2. Find the verification email from UPCAT Simulator.
3. Click the verification button.
4. Return to the app and sign in.

> If you do not verify your email, some account recovery and security actions may be limited.

### Social login options:
you can link or sign in with:
- Google
- Facebook
- LinkedIn

### Recommended setup:
even if you use social login, set a local password in Settings so you have a backup sign-in method.

### Set up your profile after first login: visit Settings and confirm:
- Full name
- Contact email
- Notification preferences
- Linked accounts

### Account security basics:

### Password
Use a strong password:
- At least 8 characters
- Uppercase +
- Lowercase -
- Number and symbol

### Recovery codes
Generate recovery codes and store them safely offline.

### Security questions
Set three questions you can remember but others cannot guess.

### Quick checklist
Task | Recommended | Where |
---|---|---|
Verify email | Yes | Inbox link | 
Link social account | Optional | Settings |
Set local password | Yes | Settings |
Generate recovery codes | Yes | Settings |
Configure notifications | Yes | Settings |
Troubleshooting | If verification email does not arrive:
1. Check spam/junk folders.
2. Wait 2-5 minutes and retry.
3. Confirm email spelling.
4. Contact support if still missing.

## Dashboard layout at a glance
The dashboard is your command center. You can start study actions, view summaries, and jump quickly to deeper analytics.
![](Dashboard Annotated Placeholder) (/help-assets/screenshots/dashboard-annotated.png)
### Main areas
#### Practice Test section
Use this for flexible practice sessions with configurable scope and pacing.
#### Mock Exam section
Use this when you want stricter simulation and readiness measurement.
#### Study Plan section
Shows your current personalized plan and today's next session.
#### Statistics preview
Displays trends and quick metrics so you can decide what to focus on next.
#### Gamification summary
Shows your XP, level, streak, and challenge progress.
#### Quick actions and shortcuts
- **Start Practice**: begin a learning-focused session.
- **Resume Session**: continue unfinished work.
- **View Stats**: inspect weak areas and trends.
- **Open Profile**: check achievements and streak status.
### Recommended dashboard routine
1. Check weak areas.
2. Run a targeted practice session.
3. Review mistakes.
4. Complete one study plan activity.
5. End with a short reflection note.
## Beginner tip
Start small and consistent. A daily 30-minute focused session usually beats irregular marathon sessions.

## What is a Mock Exam?
A Mock Exam is a realistic simulation of exam pressure and pacing.
### Practice vs Mock comparison
| Feature | Practice Test | Mock Exam |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configuration | User-defined | Admin-defined |
| Timer | Optional and pausable | Strict and non-pausable |
| Subjects | Flexible | Full exam structure |
| Navigation | Usually freer | Subtest-restricted |
| Scoring | Learning-oriented | Readiness-oriented |
### Key characteristics
- Fixed structure and rules
- Subtests with separate time limits
- Possible negative marking
- Limited retries and cooldowns
### Best time to take mock exams
- After steady practice for at least 2 weeks
- After finishing key study plan modules (1-2 weeks before your target exam date)
### Availability notes
Mock availability may be limited by plan, cooldown, or scheduling windows.

## Before you start
nChecklist:
n- Stable internet
n- Full uninterrupted time block
n- Quiet environment
n- Scratch paper and pencil
n
### Start sequence
n1. Open available mock exam.
n2. Review total duration and rules.
n3. Confirm readiness checklist.
n4. Click begin (timer starts immediately).
n
### Subtest flow
nMock exams commonly run in multiple subtests, each with separate timing.
n
### Timer warning colors
n- White: comfortable
n- Yellow: less than 10 minutes
n- Red: less than 5 minutes
n- Flashing: less than 1 minute

### Navigation rules
n- Usually you can move within current subtest.
n- Returning to previous subtests is typically not allowed.
n
### Finishing subtests
nWhen you finish a subtest, review unanswered and flagged items first because prior sections are usually locked afterward.
n
### Emergency situations
n- Connection loss: answered items are periodically synced
n- Browser crash: recover session quickly
n- Power interruption: timer usually continues server-side
n
[!warning] n> Treat mock exams like real exam events. Avoid interruptions and multitasking.

content.body:
## Overall score components
n- Raw score
n- Adjusted score (if negative marking)
n- Percentage
n- Readiness band
n
### Adjusted score formula
nAdjusted score is often calculated as: n*Adjusted = Correct -- (Incorrect * Penalty)**
Example:
n- Correct: 156
n- Incorrect: 30
n- Penalty: -0.25
n-- Adjusted: 156 -- (30 x -0.25) = -148.5

### Percentile explained
nIf you are at the 78th percentile, you scored higher than 78% of test takers in that comparison group.
n
### Predicted score
nPredicted score is an estimate, not an official result.
n
[!warning] n> Do not over-focus on one predicted value. Track trajectory across multiple mocks.
n
### Time analysis interpretation
n- Finished very early: possible rushing
n- Ran out of time: pacing issue
n- Used most time effectively: balanced pacing

### Action plan after results
n1. Identify weakest subtest.
n2. Run targeted practice.
n3. Repeat mock after focused review.

content.body:
## Time management rules
n- Budget average time per item.
n- Avoid spending over 2 minutes on one question.
n- Flag and return when possible.
n- Reserve final minutes for quick checks.
n
### Answering strategy
n- Read question stem completely first.
n- Eliminate clearly wrong choices.
n- Use keyword clues.
n- In math/science, estimate first for sanity checking.
n
### Negative marking strategy
n- If you can eliminate 2+ options, educated guessing may be favorable.
n- If no elimination is possible, skipping may be safer depending on penalty.
n
### Preparation routine before mock day
n- Take 2-3 mocks before target date.
n- Simulate real conditions.
n- Review error patterns, not just final scores.
n- Rest before high-stakes runs.

content.body:
## What is a Practice Test? A Practice Test is a configurable learning session designed for **understanding and improvement**, not pressure.
Practice Test vs Mock Exam | Aspect | Practice Test | Mock Exam |
---|---|---|
Configuration | You choose settings: Admin-defined | Timer | Optional and pausable | Strict and non-pausable |
Feedback | Can be immediate | End-only |
Purpose | Learning and skill-building | Readiness assessment |
Stress level | Low to medium | High |
## Key characteristics
- You configure almost everything.
- Timer is optional.
- Feedback can be immediate.
- Results are tracked separately from mock exams.
- Session design encourages experimentation.
## When to use practice tests
- Daily review sessions
- Weak-topic drilling
- Learning new material
- Confidence building before mock exams
[tip] Use practice tests to debug your thinking process. The goal is not just score, but clarity.
## Suggested frequency
Beginners: 4-5 short sessions weekly
Intermediate: 5-6 mixed sessions weekly
Advanced: 3-4 targeted sessions + 1 mock exam

### Step 1: Choose subjects and topics
- Pick one or more subjects.
- Optionally choose subtopics for focused drills.
- Use broad selection for variety, targeted selection for weakness repair.

### Step 2: Set question count
Range is usually **5 to 200+**.
Recommended ranges:
- Quick review: 10-20 questions (15-30 min)
- Standard session: 30-50 questions (45-75 min)
- Deep practice: 75-100 questions (90-150 min)
- Endurance: 100-200 questions (2-3 hours)
If your selected filters have fewer available questions, the system will use what is available.
### Step 3: Configure difficulty distribution
Difficulty meaning:
- **Easy**: foundational and direct
- **Medium**: multi-step reasoning
- **Hard**: high complexity and longer solving
Presets:
- Balanced: 33/34/33
- Easy-Focus: 50/35/15
- Challenge Mode: 15/35/50
You can also set custom ratios; total should equal 100%.
### Step 4: Timer settings
Why use timer?
- Trains pacing
- Simulates pressure
- Reveals speed bottlenecks
Rule of thumb: **1 to 2 minutes per question**.
### Step 5: Feedback mode
Immediate feedback is best for learning. You get correction and rationale instantly.
### After Submission
Best for simulation and concentration continuity.
### Additional options
- Shuffle questions: recommended
- Shuffle choices: recommended
- Question type blend: multiple choice, passage-based, or both
Presets and recommendations
Save successful configurations as presets. Reusing validated setups helps compare progress fairly over time.

### Interface overview
- Timer bar (if enabled)
- Progress indicator
- Question body and choices
- Previous/Next navigation
- Question grid (answered/unanswered/flagged)

### Answering questions
- Click a choice to select.
- Click again to change your selection.
- Answers are auto-saved.

### Immediate feedback flow
1. Select answer
2. See correctness
3. Read rationale
4. Move forward
Color coding:
- Green: correct
- Red: incorrect

### Flagging for review
Flags help you revisit uncertain items.
They do not affect score.
Use flags for timeboxing difficult items.

### Pausing (if timer enabled)
When paused:
- Timer stops
- Current state is preserved
- Resume continues from exact state

### Submitting
You will get a confirmation prompt, including unanswered counts if any.

### Keyboard shortcuts
1/2/3/4 or A/B/C/D: select answer
Left/Right arrow: previous/next
F: flag current question
Enter: confirm and continue
Space: pause/resume timer
If you feel stuck,
flag and move. Momentum preserves focus.

content.body:
## Timer ended before completion
### Why this happens
- Over-investing in a few difficult questions
- Slow reading pace
- Re-checking too often
### Fix plan
1. Practice with strict per-question targets.
2. Use flag-and-return strategy.
3. Review slowest subtopics.

# Lost internet during exam
- Reconnect immediately.
- Reopen session page.
- Continue if time remains.

# Score seems wrong
Check:
- Negative marking rules
- Unanswered count
- Subtest-specific scoring
If mismatch persists, submit a support ticket with session ID.

# Cannot start mock exam
Possible causes:
- Cooldown active
- Attempt limit reached
- Schedule window closed

# Payment submitted but not approved yet
Manual review can take processing time depending on queue and submission clarity.

# Forgot password and no recovery codes
Use recovery flow first, then support verification if needed.

# Blank page or app not loading
1. Hard refresh
2. Clear cached files
3. Try a different browser/network
4. Check platform status

# Question typo or content issue
Use in-app question flagging to report inaccuracies.

# Contact support
Open a ticket through the support page and include:
- account email
- issue summary
- steps to reproduce
- screenshot if available

fags.question: My exam timer ran out before I finished. What should I do?
fags.answer: Review pacing metrics in your results, then run shorter timed drills to build speed before your next full simulation.

fags.question: I lost internet during an exam.
fags.answer: Reconnect quickly and reopen your session. Most answers are auto-synced periodically.

fags.question: I forgot my password and have no recovery codes.
fags.answer: Use account recovery flow and contact support with verification details if needed.
